vm.tools.title: System Tool Replacement & Sandbox Graduation
vm.tools.info: All switches are off by default (native system tools stay open). Enabling a switch replaces that category's system tools with SA-VM sandbox tools, protected by security boundaries and sandbox policy.
vm.tools.profilesDesc: Runs only server-defined typechecks, frontend builds, or allowlisted single-test commands under sandbox protection. Never opens arbitrary bun arguments, ad-hoc scripts, path escapes, or environment variables; source directories remain limited to the current workspace.
vm.tools.draftHint: Selections only edit the draft; click Save to write them into the current thread. They take effect on the next turn (tool definitions and skill are built per turn). Policies are isolated per thread; switching conversations requires re-enabling.
vm.tools.readDesc: Off by default (system reads open): the model may use system read tools (read_file, cat, etc.) to read SKILL.md, cheat sheets, and project sources; when on, SA-VM reads are forced (vm-read).
vm.tools.writeDesc: Off by default (native system writes): the model uses native system write tools; when on, SA-VM writes are forced (vm-write), protected by workspace write directories and safety backups.
vm.tools.patchDesc: Off by default (native apply_patch): when on, native patches are intercepted and forced through the SA-VM diff patch engine (vm-patch) with safety checks and automatic backups.
vm.tools.execDesc: Off by default (regular system commands allowed): when on, host Shell / Terminal are blocked; all computation, automation, and batch work must go through the sa_vm_run sandbox.
vm.tools.jsDesc: Off by default (JS execution blocked): when on, Node / JS scripts and automation tasks may run under the VM security policy (vm-js); when off, all direct JS calls are blocked.
vm.tools.pyDesc: Off by default (Python execution blocked): when on, Python scripts may run under the VM security policy (vm-py); when off, all direct Python calls are blocked.
vm.tools.bunTitle: Allow Controlled Bun Execution (Safe Bun Runner)
vm.tools.bunDesc: Off by default: when on, the model may run constrained general Bun commands in the workspace sandbox (test, build, run-a-file directly, restricted --filter; no package installs, no arbitrary shell scripts, no package.json script escapes).
vm.tools.clearTitle: Let Model Prune Stale Tool History (Clear Tool History)
vm.tools.clearDesc: Off by default (exploratory): grants the model the clear_tool_history action. In long conversations the model may replace outdated read/search outputs with short placeholders, freeing context tokens and extending memory.
vm.tools.refsTitle: Find All Symbol References (Find All References)
vm.tools.refsDesc: Off by default (exploratory): grants the model the find_references action. Precisely finds symbol definitions (e0), imports (e1), and calls (e2) across the project with unique paths and zero duplication, built-in count caps (max_results), token circuit breaker (max_tokens), and candidate-file targeted search.
vm.savings.title: Context Savings
vm.savings.info: All switches are off by default (behavior unchanged). An optimization takes effect only when enabled; they apply per thread and never interfere across threads.
vm.savings.opt1Desc: Large read_file requests over the threshold are auto-rejected (default 50KB), steering toward read_lines / find_references.
vm.savings.opt2Desc: Over-limit results are truncated and marked; when tokens overflow only paths and line numbers return.
vm.savings.opt3Title: OPT-3 Slim test and build output
vm.savings.opt3Desc: Success returns only key summary lines; failures keep full diagnostics.
vm.savings.opt4Desc: Batches with more than K full read_file requests are rejected outright; oversized single items (>20KB) and over-budget totals are truncated and marked.
vm.savings.opt9Desc: Identical calls in one batch execute once; results are shared and marked.
vm.savings.opt5Desc: Full injection on the first turn, summaries after; write-related sections expand on demand.
vm.savings.opt6Desc: Folds only mid-turn events in model-facing turn history; UI display and archives stay intact.
vm.savings.opt7Desc: Read-only outputs older than N turns become summary placeholders; writes never fold, only the model view changes.

jev.enhance.keyHint: No API key in the JEV settings panel yet: calls below will be rejected (JEV is not configured) even if enabled. Fill Base URL / Key / model in the JEV smart review settings first.
jev.enhance.chooseDesc: Lets the model call JEV single-choice verdict at branch points; when off the skill no longer suggests it and direct calls are rejected with capability_denied.
jev.enhance.checklistDesc: Lets the model call JEV multi-item self-check before delivery; when off the skill no longer suggests it and direct calls are rejected with capability_denied.
jev.enhance.evaluateDesc: Lets the model pass custom questions through for SystemOne eval; off by default, enable on demand.
jev.enhance.thinkingDesc: Lets the model list candidate approaches for JEV single-choice before long thinking, with a direct-action brake; one call per round. Advisory only, never blocks thinking.
jev.enhance.redteamDesc: Before risky moves (migrations, auth, security boundaries), hands the plan to JEV for holes: most likely failure point plus ship / harden-first / stop verdict, covering blind spots the model missed.
jev.enhance.rankDesc: Ranks 2–6 candidates by a given criterion (e.g. ROI) and returns the top three: use it to order tech-debt and refactor backlogs by value; unranked items keep their original order.
jev.enhance.scopeDesc: Reviews whether the scope is deliverable in one go (fits / split / merge) at planning time, then points at the weakest phase when candidates are given, avoiding oversized tasks started blind.
jev.enhance.dispatchDesc: Must pass before fanning out to subagents/Tasks: returns solo / parallel / serial / batch strategy plus weakest link, concurrency and dispatch plan; execute per plan.
jev.enhance.consistencyDesc: Audits whether the plan itself violates hard constraints, item by item (holds / violated / unclear); unlike evidence-checking checklist, fits constraint-heavy plans that resist enumeration.
jev.enhance.doneDesc: Checks before claiming done: original request vs actual work vs verification evidence; cures fake deliveries with leftover TODOs, missing verification or drifted scope. Ship only on pass.
jev.enhance.diagnoseDesc: On errors, judges the most likely true cause first, then whether the proposed fix cures, mitigates or masks it; pass this gate before symptomatic fixes and stop slapping on optional chaining.
jev.enhance.edgeCasesDesc: Hands the implementation to JEV to flag the 1–2 weakest spots across numeric / null-and-default / encoding / reentrancy / interruption edges, then add assertions; do not test only the happy path.
jev.enhance.blastRadiusDesc: Reviews side effects and the merge verdict before landing important diffs; note: red-team for plans, blast for diffs, do not mix them.
jev.enhance.intentDesc: Judges intent right after user input: single most-likely reading plus clarity verdict when candidates are given, otherwise classifies into the built-in 8 intent types (clear / needs follow-up / needs confirm) with a suggested first step.
jev.enhance.nextDesc: Do not idle after a task: picks the best next step plus momentum verdict when candidates are given, otherwise judges continue-directly / confirm-first / wrap-up from backlog context.
jev.enhance.compressDesc: Runs gated per-thread compression: checklist gate, then add_memory externalization, then clear_tool_history. Subscription mode trims small and often; token mode trims at threshold.
jev.enhance.progressDesc: Checks progress on demand while a task runs: progress band (0–25/25–50/50–75/75–99/100) plus on-track / risk / blocked / done plus next step. Trigger manually only for big refactors / multi-phase work, not every round.
jev.enhance.memoryDesc: Judges whether a candidate fact should be skipped, saved for this workspace, or kept across workspaces; use add_memory for facts worth saving.
